mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past month signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2% does not correlate with negative 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past month signals weakening labor market conditions, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase > 0.5pp does not correlate with negative 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the past two months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic demand weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or HOUST decline > 5% does not correlate with negative 60-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past month signals strengthening supply-side conditions, which typically leads to increased economic activity and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 1% does not correlate with positive 5-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, it signals a tightening monetary policy in the face of inflationary pressures, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with negative 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 over the past month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or PAYEMS decrease > 100,000 does not correlate with negative 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) decline by more than 1% over the past month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.3 percentage points, it signals a weakening demand coupled with labor market stress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with negative 60-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past three months signals an easing monetary policy, which typically leads to lower borrowing costs and increased investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease > 0.5pp does not correlate with positive 20-day returns (p > 0.05).
